transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I’ve started doing things that scare me. Like walking out in the middle of a deployment, or driving around late at night with no real plan. That’s not how I’ve ever handled stress before.
Have you had a period where you felt unusually high, energized, or irritable compared with your normal self?
No, I haven’t noticed feeling unusually high or full of energy like that. I’ve been more unsettled than anything.
Do you have nightmares or unwanted memories about something traumatic that happened to you?

Yes. Out of nowhere, especially near that conference area or if someone raises their voice on a call, I get hit with images and sounds from that night. It’s so strong I lose track of what I was saying.
Do you avoid places or situations that remind you of what happened?
Yes. I take the long way around the building so I don’t have to go near that floor. And if people start talking about the contractor or the cutover, I usually shut the conversation down right away.
Since that happened, have you been feeling constantly on guard or easily startled?
Yes. If a door slams, my phone rings suddenly, or someone comes up behind my chair, I jerk really hard. My hands shake afterward, and it takes me a few minutes to settle down and look normal again.
Since that happened, have you felt emotionally numb or cut off from other people?
Yeah. My husband will hug me or tell me he’s proud of me, and I know—I know I love him, but I don’t feel that warmth I used to. It just doesn’t come through.
Have these symptoms been going on for more than a month?
Yes. It started after that late-night cutover incident—it's been about 13 months now.
Since that incident, have you been blaming yourself for what happened?
Yes. I keep thinking I should have handled it better. Even on quiet days, there’s this fear and shame sitting in my chest, like something could still happen if I let my guard down.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not really sure. I’ve been struggling, but I don’t know if I’d call it feeling depressed most of the day, every day.
Have you been having thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life?
No, I haven’t had thoughts about hurting myself or ending my life.
Outside of this recent stress, have you often acted impulsively in ways that ended up hurting you?

Not usually, no. This is new for me. Lately I’ve walked out in the middle of deployments, or driven around late at night with no real destination. It scares me because that’s not how I’ve ever dealt with stress before.
When you’ve walked out during deployments or driven around late at night, does it usually happen right after something reminds you of that incident?

I don’t know if it’s always right after a reminder. I just know I’ve been doing things that scare me—walking out during deployments or driving around late at night with no plan—and that’s really not how I’ve handled stress before.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah. I used to plan my week around salsa, book club, yoga, or having people over to make Guatemalan food. Now I mostly cancel and just sit at home scrolling on my phone or pretending to watch a show.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah. Most nights I’m lying there replaying parts of what happened at the office. When I finally fall asleep, I wake up tense—from dreams sometimes, or even a small noise. I’m exhausted before work even starts.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt sad, empty, or hopeless most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I’ve been having a hard time, but I don’t know if I’d say I’ve felt sad or hopeless most of every day.
Over the past two weeks, have you been feeling worthless nearly every day?
I’m not sure I’d say worthless, no. I’ve been struggling, but I haven’t really thought of myself that way.
When you walk out during deployments or drive around late at night, do you feel detached from yourself or like things around you aren’t real?
I don’t think so. When I’m out walking or driving, I feel like I’m there and things are real around me.
Since this started, have you been taking more risks than usual?
Yes. I’ve started doing things that scare me—walking out in the middle of deployments, or driving around late at night with no plan. That’s not how I’ve ever handled stress before.
Do these late-night drives or walking out during deployments feel like a way to escape the distress from what happened that night?
I think so, yes. I don’t really have a plan when I leave—I just walk out or drive around. It feels like I need to get away from it for a while.
Since this started, have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yes. It’s showing up at work—I was told in my review that I’m missing important handoffs, leaving meetings abruptly, and making the team have to work around me. And at home, my husband says I’m barely present anymore.
